summary.headline: Sobha Q1 FY27 record presales of INR3,656 crore (+76% YoY) and PAT of INR50.7 crore vs INR13.5 crore a year earlier.
summary.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly real estate sales of INR3,656 crore on 2.34 million sq ft and 1,432 homes, at an average realisation of INR15,655 per sq ft. Total income rose about 48% YoY to INR1,330 crore and real estate revenue rose about 60% to INR1,107 crore. Net cash stood at INR659 crore, with operational cash inflow of INR1,924 crore, though collections lagged presales because new-sale cash came late in the quarter and milestone billing slipped on labour shortages in April and May. Management reiterated margin recovery from H2 FY27, with EBITDA guided to 17-20% by Q4 from 9.7% currently.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Contributed 57% of quarterly sales (about INR2,067 crore), driven by SOBHA One World and Sacred Grove plotted development. One World: 3,484 homes on 47.4 acres, 3.4 million sq ft released, about 40% sold at launch.

segments.name: NCR
segments.commentary: Record quarterly sales of about INR1,384 crore, mainly from SOBHA Crescent in Gurgaon, where about 60% was sold in Q1.

segments.name: Contractual, manufacturing and retail
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR171 crore; management expects FY27 other-business revenue similar to FY26. Commercial rental income about INR23 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales growth of at least 30% guided; could be slightly better if all launches happen on time.
FY27 completions targeted at 6-6.5 million sq ft vs 5.4 million sq ft in FY26 (about 20% higher).
Launch of 9 projects, about 8.2 million sq ft (about INR12,000 crore GDV at about INR15,000 crore per 1 million sq ft basis) in the remaining nine months; roughly 3 projects in Q2, rest in Q3 and Q4.
Net debt expected to be around zero for FY27.
Operating cash flow of about INR2,000 crore is an average run rate over the next few years, expected to be touched as the company grows.
EBITDA at 9.7% currently, targeted at 17-20% by end of Q4 FY27; Q2 similar to Q1, with Q3 and Q4 improving as high-margin projects complete.
Land payments in FY27 expected at about INR1,500-1,600 crore if pending Bangalore and NCR deals close (about INR370 crore spent so far; FY26 was about INR1,160 crore).
capex_capacity: Launched 3 projects in Bangalore and Gurgaon in Q1 with combined saleable area of 6.89 million sq ft and potential sales value of about INR10,000 crore.
Forthcoming pipeline of 20.77 million sq ft across 17 projects; 14.94 million sq ft unsold inventory at end-Q1.
Q1 capex about INR70 crore and land investment about INR370 crore (new land in Mumbai, about 1.3 acres for about INR180 crore, and a Greater Noida joint development).
Crescent Phase 2 (NCR) expected around end-Q3 or start-Q4 FY27.
Greater Noida project GDV about INR2,700-3,000 crore combined with the Mumbai site; Greater Noida launch targeted this FY, Mumbai timeline uncertain and excluded from the 8.2 million sq ft pipeline.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand strong, with preparation time before launches cited as the driver; management described the overall demand as steady post-launch.
Rivana (Noida) sales steady monthly and quarterly, without a high sell-through at launch.

Revenue recognition backlog of INR20,553 crore yet to be recognised on sold projects; projected receivables and unsold value about INR31,000 crore against remaining cost of about INR19,000 crore, implying about INR12,000 crore margin cash flow.
Some INR200-300 crore of One World sales may spill into Q2 recognition, per the analyst's arithmetic that management did not dispute.
Forthcoming pipeline margin of INR68.3 billion, down from about INR86 billion previously, due to a higher joint development mix and lower own-land exposure (Hoskote).

qa_highlights.question: What presales growth and launch GDV are expected for FY27, and which projects come next?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 30% presales growth guided; about 9 projects, 8.2 million sq ft, in the remaining nine months, with about 3 projects in Q2 and the rest in Q3-Q4. Roughly INR12,000 crore GDV from the 8.2 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Why were collections modest versus presales?
qa_highlights.answer: New-sale collections came late in the quarter, and milestone billing was lower because some milestones were missed due to labour shortages in April and May.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the forthcoming-project margin fall from about INR86 billion to INR68.3 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Greater mix of joint development projects, and Hoskote (own land, high margin) dropped from the forthcoming set.

qa_highlights.question: Land spend and business development plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 land spend about INR1,160 crore; FY27 about INR370 crore so far, with INR600-700 crore more identified (mostly Bangalore, rest NCR and Mumbai). Total could reach INR1,500-1,600 crore. Land typically about 15% of sales value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the demand recovery in the second half of the quarter, and what about Rivana?
qa_highlights.answer: Preparation time for launches drove the stronger response; demand described as steady. Rivana sales steady with no spike at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 similar to Q1; Q3 and Q4 sequentially better as high-margin projects complete. EBITDA to move from 9.7% to 17-20% by Q4.

risks_watch: Labour shortages in April-May delayed milestones and billing; collections and cash flow depend on the milestone schedule.
Mumbai site approvals and timing are uncertain; Greater Noida is planned for FY27.
Karnataka minimum wage hike of about 60% in May 2026; cost impact still under assessment, management expects absorption within budget.
Margin recovery to 17-20% by Q4 depends on high-margin completions; Q2 flat.
NCD issue of INR1,000 crore approved, to be drawn in at least 2 tranches tied to land deals.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sales momentum and launch pipeline, with specific numbers on guidance. More measured on collections and margins, which management attributed to timing and labour constraints. Evasive on the Gurgaon commercial project, which has been removed from the pipeline and is being evaluated for rental retention.
key_quotes: We achieved our highest ever quarterly real estate sales, recording sales value of INR3,656 crores, representing 76% increase year-on-year.
We would see margin expansion as we complete the projects that we have sold from FY '23.
So, our expectation is that by Q4, as we currently, we are at about 9.7% EBITDA. So, as we leave the end of Q4, maybe hopefully, we should be able to do closer towards 17% to 20%.
